cut_items.item: Docker Engine 25+ caveat: --volumes only removes anonymous volumes, so a separate `docker volume prune -a -f` is needed to remove named volumes
Explicit stop of running containers before pruning (docker stop $(docker ps -q)) as the first step in the main flow
Pruning with -f skips confirmation, used directly in the main command
Docker Engine 25+ `--volumes` on prune removes only anonymous volumes, so named volumes may remain and `docker volume prune -a -f` is needed to remove them
Stops running containers first (`docker stop $(docker ps -q)`) so prune also removes their resources, which gives a one-sequence full cleanup

added_items.item: Explains that plain prune keeps running containers and the images, volumes, and networks they use (safe/unused-only mode vs. delete-everything mode)
Interactive confirmation prompt (type y) and that -f skips it
Explicit build cache clearing command for the manual route: docker builder prune -a -f
Troubleshooting: a volume in use is refused, so remove the container that uses it first
Docker Desktop on Mac/Windows: disk image file may not shrink after cleanup; reduce disk image size in Settings > Resources or use Troubleshoot menu clean up data
To keep volumes, omit --volumes from the prune command
Manual route uses `docker ps -aq` for stop, covering all containers including stopped ones
Lists exactly what the prune command removes in a per-item breakdown (the -a flag meaning, the --volumes flag meaning)
Distinguishes a prune-unused path (keeps running containers and the resources they use) from a delete-everything path, so the reader can pick the safer option
Lists exactly what `docker system prune -a --volumes` removes (stopped containers, unused networks, unused images, unused volumes, build cache) and that running containers and what they use are kept
The `-f` flag skips the confirmation prompt (without `-f` Docker asks for `y`)
Explicit command to stop and remove all containers (`docker stop` then `docker rm -f`)
Explicit `docker builder prune -a -f` to clear the build cache
Troubleshooting: a volume in use cannot be removed until its container is removed
Docker Desktop (Mac/Windows): the disk image file may not shrink after cleanup; reduce the disk image size in Settings > Resources or use the Troubleshoot menu to clean up
